title: The Performance Effects of Giving Front-Line Employees Direct Access to Performance Data and Thereby Limiting the Supervisor’s Feedback-Intermediation Role: Evidence from a Field Experiment
authors: Ethan Scott Bernstein; Shelley Xin Li
eligible_reason: Randomized field experiment with a single intervention date: employees' time-use analytics were made available to the treatment group simultaneously. Table 3 cols 1-3 are pooled OLS DiD (trxpost, Treatment, post) with pre-period outcome and survey controls; cols 4-6 and Tables 4-7 add employee FE with a common post indicator (subsamples split by moderators). Not staggered; data not shipped (confidentiality agreement).
design_notes: Employee-day panel (xtset EmployeeID StartDate); trxpost = Treatment x post with one common post date; clustered by orgid.
data_files_note: ReplicationCode.do: data cannot be disclosed under the field site's confidentiality agreement; only code and a replication appendix are shipped.
